questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Component Inputs”?
options: Component Inputs helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
Component Inputs means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Component Inputs removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
Component Inputs should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
questions.answer_key: Component Inputs helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Component Inputs is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Passing data from parent to child” in this lesson?
options: Treat “Passing data from parent to child” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
Assume “Passing data from parent to child” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “Passing data from parent to child” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
Connect “Passing data from parent to child” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Passing data from parent to child” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Passing data from parent to child” under Component Inputs. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Component Inputs”?
options: Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
